instruction:
Parse this nginx access log line into JSON with keys ip, time, method, path, protocol, status, bytes, referer, user_agent:
203.0.113.45 - - [12/Oct/2023:14:05:07 +0000] "GET /api/v1/items?limit=20 HTTP/1.1" 200 1432 "-" "curl/8.4.0"

Extract method, path, status and bytes from this nginx log line as JSON:
198.51.100.22 - - [12/Oct/2023:14:06:11 +0000] "POST /api/v1/orders HTTP/1.1" 201 512 "https://shop.example.com/checkout" "Mozilla/5.0 (X11; Linux x86_64; rv:118.0)"

Parse this nginx line and return only the status code and requested path as JSON:
192.0.2.10 - - [12/Oct/2023:14:07:22 +0000] "GET /static/img/logo.png HTTP/1.1" 404 153 "https://example.com/home" "Mozilla/5.0 (Macintosh; Intel Mac OS X 10_15_7)"
Write a regex with named groups (ip, method, path, status) that matches an nginx combined log line

This nginx uses a custom format with a trailing rt field. Parse the line into JSON including request_time as a number:
10.0.0.7 - - [12/Oct/2023:14:08:33 +0000] "GET /healthz HTTP/1.1" 200 2 "-" "Prometheus/2.45.0" rt=0.003

Parse this nginx line where the byte count is missing. Represent missing bytes as null in JSON:
192.0.2.55 - - [12/Oct/2023:14:09:01 +0000] "HEAD /status HTTP/1.1" 200 - "-" "uptime-robot/2.0"

Parse this nginx line with an IPv6 client address into JSON with ip, method, path, status:
2001:db8::1 - - [12/Oct/2023:14:10:12 +0000] "GET /index.html HTTP/1.1" 304 0 "-" "Mozilla/5.0"

Parse this nginx line and split the request target into a path field and a query object as JSON:
192.0.2.31 - - [12/Oct/2023:14:11:00 +0000] "GET /search?q=prometheus+grafana&page=2 HTTP/1.1" 200 8432 "-" "Mozilla/5.0"
Write a Python function using the re module that parses an nginx combined log line and returns a dict, or None when the line does not match
Write a grok pattern that parses the nginx combined log format into named fields

Parse this nginx line with upstream timing fields into JSON, keeping uct, uht and urt as numbers:
10.0.0.9 - - [12/Oct/2023:14:12:45 +0000] "POST /api/v1/checkout HTTP/1.1" 500 231 "-" "python-requests/2.31.0" uct=0.045 uht=0.044 urt=0.044

Parse these three nginx access log lines into a JSON array of objects with ip, status and path:
10.0.0.1 - - [12/Oct/2023:14:13:01 +0000] "GET /a HTTP/1.1" 200 100 "-" "curl/8.4.0"
10.0.0.2 - - [12/Oct/2023:14:13:02 +0000] "POST /b HTTP/1.1" 403 88 "-" "curl/8.4.0"
10.0.0.3 - - [12/Oct/2023:14:13:03 +0000] "DELETE /c HTTP/1.1" 500 210 "-" "curl/8.4.0"

Among these three lines, find the one that is not a valid nginx combined log line and return it as JSON:
192.0.2.1 - - [12/Oct/2023:14:15:01 +0000] "GET /one HTTP/1.1" 200 10 "-" "curl/8.4.0"
this line is broken and has no request
192.0.2.2 - - [12/Oct/2023:14:15:03 +0000] "GET /two HTTP/1.1" 200 20 "-" "curl/8.4.0"
output: {"invalid_line": "this line is broken and has no request", "position": 2}

instruction:
Parse this nginx line with an HTTP/1.0 request and a percent encoded path into JSON:
192.0.2.77 - - [12/Oct/2023:14:16:58 +0000] "GET /download/report%202023.pdf HTTP/1.0" 200 54321 "-" "Wget/1.21"

Nginx logs the X-Forwarded-For header first. Parse this line and return the forwarded chain and the direct client as JSON:
172.16.0.4, 203.0.113.8 - - [12/Oct/2023:14:17:40 +0000] "GET /api/me HTTP/1.1" 200 891 "-" "okhttp/4.11.0"

Sum the response bytes across these nginx lines and return total_bytes and request_count as JSON. Treat a dash byte field as zero:
10.0.1.1 - - [12/Oct/2023:14:19:01 +0000] "GET /a HTTP/1.1" 200 1432 "-" "curl/8.4.0"
10.0.1.2 - - [12/Oct/2023:14:19:02 +0000] "GET /b HTTP/1.1" 200 2048 "-" "curl/8.4.0"
10.0.1.3 - - [12/Oct/2023:14:19:03 +0000] "GET /c HTTP/1.1" 304 - "-" "curl/8.4.0"
10.0.1.4 - - [12/Oct/2023:14:19:04 +0000] "POST /d HTTP/1.1" 500 231 "-" "curl/8.4.0"

Compute the average rt value across these nginx lines with a custom format and return JSON rounded to 3 decimals:
10.0.2.1 - - [12/Oct/2023:14:20:01 +0000] "GET /a HTTP/1.1" 200 10 "-" "curl/8.4.0" rt=0.020
10.0.2.2 - - [12/Oct/2023:14:20:02 +0000] "GET /b HTTP/1.1" 200 10 "-" "curl/8.4.0" rt=0.040
10.0.2.3 - - [12/Oct/2023:14:20:03 +0000] "GET /c HTTP/1.1" 200 10 "-" "curl/8.4.0" rt=0.060

Parse this classic common log format line (with ident and user fields) into JSON:
127.0.0.1 - frank [12/Oct/2023:14:21:07 +0000] "GET /apache_pb.gif HTTP/1.0" 200 2326
